property_summary: After calling C.initialize() twice (once via a program operator after first initializing C), the reference version's initializer modifier prevents re-initialization and thus the second call to initialize() is reverted; the buggy version allows re-initialization, so the second call succeeds, and reading the public variable initialized version via the _getInitializedVersion() internal function is not available, but the state variable _initialized is private. The observable difference is that in the reference, a call to C.initialize() after the first initialization will revert, whereas in the buggy version it will not revert. The concrete scenario: deploy C, then call c.initialize() (first call), then call c.initialize() again; the reference reverts on the second call, the buggy version does not. The assertion uses try/catch around the second initialize call to capture the revert behavior.
change_summary: Remove the require that checks _initialized < 1 to allow repeated initialization.
